## Answer

**Yes**, the first-order weak derivative of $f$ belongs to $W^{-k-1,p}(X)$. Here is the justification.

### Setup and Definitions

Let $X$ be the spatial domain (an open set, here regarded as a Banach space) and let $1 < p < \infty$ with conjugate exponent $q$ satisfying $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1$. The negative Sobolev space is defined by duality:

$$W^{-k,p}(X) := \bigl(W^{k,q}_0(X)\bigr)^*,$$

i.e., the continuous dual of $W^{k,q}_0(X)$. An element $f \in W^{-k,p}(X)$ is a bounded linear functional on $W^{k,q}_0(X)$, and its norm is

$$\|f\|_{W^{-k,p}} = \sup_{\substack{\varphi \in W^{k,q}_0(X)\\ \|\varphi\|_{W^{k,q}}\le 1}} |\langle f, \varphi\rangle|.$$

### Distributional Derivative

For any distribution $f$ and any test function $\varphi \in C_c^\infty(X)$, the first-order weak (distributional) derivative $\partial_i f$ is defined by

$$\langle \partial_i f,\, \varphi\rangle := -\langle f,\, \partial_i \varphi\rangle.$$

We must show that this extends to a bounded linear functional on $W^{k+1,q}_0(X)$, which would prove $\partial_i f \in (W^{k+1,q}_0(X))^* = W^{-k-1,p}(X)$.

### Key Estimate

Take $\varphi \in W^{k+1,q}_0(X)$. Since $\varphi \in W^{k+1,q}_0(X)$, its derivative $\partial_i \varphi$ belongs to $W^{k,q}_0(X)$ (differentiation maps $W^{k+1,q}_0$ into $W^{k,q}_0$), and by the definition of the Sobolev norm,

$$\|\partial_i \varphi\|_{W^{k,q}} \leq \|\varphi\|_{W^{k+1,q}}.$$

Now compute, using $f \in W^{-k,p}(X) = (W^{k,q}_0(X))^*$:

$$|\langle \partial_i f,\, \varphi\rangle| = |\langle f,\, \partial_i \varphi\rangle| \leq \|f\|_{W^{-k,p}}\;\|\partial_i \varphi\|_{W^{k,q}} \leq \|f\|_{W^{-k,p}}\;\|\varphi\|_{W^{k+1,q}}.$$

### Conclusion

The estimate

$$|\langle \partial_i f,\, \varphi\rangle| \leq \|f\|_{W^{-k,p}}\;\|\varphi\|_{W^{k+1,q}}, \qquad \forall\, \varphi \in W^{k+1,q}_0(X),$$

shows that $\partial_i f$ extends to a bounded linear functional on $W^{k+1,q}_0(X)$. By definition, this means

$$\partial_i f \in \bigl(W^{k+1,q}_0(X)\bigr)^* = W^{-k-1,p}(X),$$

with the norm bound

$$\|\partial_i f\|_{W^{-k-1,p}} \leq \|f\|_{W^{-k,p}}.$$

**The answer is yes.** The essential reason is that differentiation is a bounded operator $W^{k+1,q}_0(X) \to W^{k,q}_0(X)$, and by duality this induces a bounded operator $W^{-k,p}(X) \to W^{-k-1,p}(X)$. Taking a weak derivative of a negative-order Sobolev distribution lowers the order by one, which is precisely the expected behavior.

### PROOF COMPLETE
